summary: Ephemeral unpin during canary weight smoothing caused subset of requests to hit fallback model
description:
Issue summary: During a canary ramp for Nimbus Health on a dedicated pool (prod-us-west), roughly 10-15% of user requests that were expected to remain pinned to rwd-7b-v2 briefly routed to the fallback model rwd-7b-quant-v2 for ~3 minutes while a canary weight change was applied.

Impact: Customer reported degraded output quality and intermittently higher token counts for affected requests. Incident caused disruption to a single customer (dedicated) and triggered an internal postmortem.

Environment: prod-us-west, dedicated GPU pool id: dp-9, rollout id: rollout-2026-03-11-nimbus-canary.

Steps to reproduce (approx):
1) Create a canary rollout with a pinned model mapping for customer route (pin->rwd-7b-v2).
2) Trigger a weight change that ramps canary from 5% to 30% over a short window (<60s).
3) Observe routing decisions and model assignment logs for requests from the customer.

Observed behavior: During the rapid ramp, the routing layer reported temporary weight=0 for the pinned model in the smoothing computation, causing evaluation to hit the fallback model for a subset of requests. The behavior stopped when the smoothing window completed and normal pinned routing resumed.

Expected behavior: A pinned model should remain pinned to the route for the customer regardless of smoothing applied to unpinned canary weights; smoothing should not reduce a pinned model's effective weight to zero.

Temporary workaround applied: Support re-applied an explicit strong pin via the admin API (pin-override) and paused the automated ramp for the rollout. Customers were advised to hold canary weight changes until the hotfix was deployed.

investigation_notes: Key findings: rollout-manager introduced a moving-average smoothing pass (window=60s) that was applied globally to route weights. A recent change intended to reduce abrupt traffic shifts applied smoothing before the pin-protection check, which allowed the smoothed weight for pinned entries to transiently drop to 0 when the canary weight changed quickly. Routing code treats weight==0 as candidate for fallback selection, which led to requests being routed to the fallback model. Route cache TTL was 5s and contributed to propagation delay for corrected routing decisions but was not the primary cause. Reproduction: replayed canary ramp in staging with identical timing and confirmed pinned entry observed weight==0 in routing diagnostics. Logs of interest: routing.decisions (trace-0a1b2c), rollout-manager.metrics (pin_evictions=3), serving-runtime.trace (serve-req-98765).
resolution_notes: Immediate action: rolled back the recent smoothing change and released a hotfix (rollout-manager v1.12.4) that applies smoothing only to unpinned routes and enforces a minimum-clamp check for pinned entries. Also added an assertion in the routing path that prevents pinned routes from being set to zero by smoothing. Deployed hotfix to prod and verified with controlled ramp and customer traffic. Added an alert (pin_eviction_rate > 0.5% for 1m) and extended routing trace retention for 72 hours after any canary ramp. Follow-ups: create INT ticket to add end-to-end test covering rapid ramp + pin, update rollout design doc, and review billing impact for Nimbus Health. Related PRs: rollout-manager#842 (hotfix), serving-runtime#2190 (additional logging).
